newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shares end down, led by blue chip falls.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shares end down, led by blue chip falls.

text.p: Selling in blue chips and large capitalisation shares overcame an upbeat start led by small-caps and second-tier shares, pushing the market lower for most of Monday's trading, brokers said.
The composite stock index provisionally ended the day down 7.23 points to 774.26. Declining shares beat advancers 528 to 306, while volume was thin at 17.09 million.

Profit-taking was strong after sharp rises near the end of last week. Brokers said fluctuation was expected until the government announces scheduled steps to expand the foreign shareholders' ceiling to 20 percent from 18 percent at present.
Blue-chip stocks were also pressured by the release of figures showing that August's trade deficit was at a monthly record high of $2.9 billion against $901 million a year ago.

Fears of an oversupply of shares also lingered. Five firms will hold initial public offerings this week, and the government has said it plans to sell large chunks of stock in Korea Telecom and other state-run companies this year.

"The index fell because of worries about the trade deficit and the government's denial of rumours that it will postpone plans to sell shares in state-run companies," said Coryo Securities broker Oh Chul-hwan.
Despite the index fall, some second-tier shares rose because margin trading in secondary stocks began Monday as scheduled.

Sammi gained 20 won to 3,200 and Yuyang Information and Communication rose 1,800 won to 61,400. Jungil Industries reached its limit high of 33,000 won before falling victim to profit taking. It ended down 1,500 won at 29,700.
Samsung Electronics bucked the blue chip down trend to rise 100 won to 61,500, on active foreign buying.
The September futures contract ended down 1.40 points to 83.70, while the KOSPI 200 index fell 0.94 point to 82.87.
